app.title: Greenline
app.tagline: Crop rotation planning with NASA Earth data
app.sampleNotice: Showing sample data for a demo field. Not real measurements yet.

common.judgmentNote: This tool supports your judgment and your local experts. It does not replace them.
common.noField: Pick your field first. Then this page will fill in.

picker.hint: Tap crops in the order you plant them. Tap a crop above to remove it.

pick.title: Pick your field
pick.intro: Find your field on the map and tap it.
pick.mapHint: Tap anywhere in North Texas. We load the nearest of 201 sampled crop fields.
pick.mapOffline: The map needs internet. You can still load the demo field.
pick.privacy: We save a 30 m map square, never your exact location.
pick.emptySummary: Tap your field on the map, or load the demo field (real NASA data) to try the app.
pick.nearest: Nearest sampled field ({id}), {km} km from your tap. Real data for every field is coming.
pick.fallback: We couldn’t load real data for this field, so this is the fake sample field.

farm.title: Your farm
farm.intro: Three quick steps. Your answers stay on this phone.
farm.step2Hint: Pick one or more. These count double in the score.
farm.waterSource: Where does your water come from?
farm.market: Where do you sell or use your crops?

story.title: Your field's history
story.headline: Your field sits bare about {months} months a year.
story.headlineDetail: Usually {months}. Bare ground loses soil and water to wind and heavy rain.
story.chartCaption: Each bar is one year, colored by year type. Recent drought years: {years}.
story.chartAlt: Bar chart of yearly rain from {from} to {to}. Average about {avg} inches. Drought years: {years}.
story.bareTitle: Green, residue or bare: 40 years from space
story.bareCaption: Each row is a year (newest on top), each square a month. The number is that year’s ground cover score.
story.doubleCropNote: The crop map says two crops this year. Low confidence: too few examples to check.
story.timelineNote: Crop names start in 2008 (USDA crop maps). Satellites changed in 2013 (Landsat 8), which reads a bit greener, so recent years may look less bare than they were.
story.replayCaption: The worst years in 40 years of NASA weather, picked by our year-pattern model. Tap one to see what happened on this field.
story.replaySoil: Soil moisture {pct}% vs. this field’s normal
story.replayNoStress: Greenness stayed near normal all season
story.coverChartTitle: Your ground cover, year by year
story.coverChartCaption: Each bar is one year. Green is time with plants growing, tan is partly covered, and the brown striped part is bare ground.
story.coverChartAlt: Bar chart of ground cover from {from} to {to}. Bare ground averaged {bare}% of the clear months since {since}.
story.sensorNote: In 2013 the satellite changed, and the newer one reads a bit greener. Bare time before 2013 may look higher than it was, so compare across that line with care.
story.typicalTitle: A typical year on your field
story.typicalCaption: Chance the ground is bare in each month, from the years since {since}.
story.partlyNote: “Partly covered” means sparse plants, stubble or crop residue. Satellites can’t yet tell these apart.

compare.title: Compare rotations
compare.intro: Scores are out of 100, based on your goals and limits. Higher fits better.
compare.glanceHint: Open each option below to see why it scored that way.
compare.noCurrent: Tell us what you grow now to compare against it.
compare.buildHint: Pick crops in order. We score it the same way as the options above.

handoff.title: Summary for your extension agent
handoff.intro: Print this page or save it as a PDF. Bring it to your county AgriLife Extension office.
questions: Do these crops fit our local market and seed supply?
What planting dates and seeding rates work here?
Are there cost-share programs (like NRCS EQIP) for cover crops?
What risks am I missing for this field?
handoff.sampleNote: This summary uses sample data, not measurements from this field.

explain.nitrogen: A legume pulls nitrogen out of the air and leaves some for the next crop.
explain.cover: A cover crop keeps living roots or residue on the soil between cash crops.
explain.deepRoots: Two or more deep-rooted crops open up the subsoil so water and roots can go deeper.
explain.diverse: Three or more different crops, so no single pest, disease or bad season hits everything.
explain.droughtTolerant: Every crop grown here handles dry spells well (low drought sensitivity).
explain.pestBreak: Grass crops and broadleaf crops take turns, which interrupts pests and diseases that build up on one plant family. Cover crops and fallow are not counted.

reasons.ryeDryYear: Texas Tech research in drought-hit West Texas: rye was the most reliable winter cover crop. It yielded even in a dry year and didn't reduce soil water for the next summer crop.
reasons.waterAvg: Average water need is {value} out of 5.
reasons.droughtHistory: {count} of the last {total} years were drought years on this field.
reasons.erosionAvg: Soil protection is {value} out of 5 on average.
reasons.slopeBare: Your {slope}% slope makes bare seasons riskier.
reasons.nitrogen: {count} season(s) with a crop that adds nitrogen.
reasons.cashShare: {count} of {total} seasons have a crop you can sell.
reasons.forageAvg: Grazing and hay value is {value} out of 5.
reasons.drySoilYears: Soil was at least 10% drier than normal in {count} of {total} growing seasons.
reasons.lowOrganicMatter: Topsoil organic matter is low ({om}%), so cover crops and legumes help more.
reasons.rotationBare: We estimate this rotation leaves the soil bare about {days} days a year.
reasons.bareCalibrated: For {crops}, the estimate uses this field's own satellite record.

gaps.budgetVariety: {count} different crops may be costly to start with a low budget.
gaps.cdlNoise: Crop history comes from USDA satellite crop maps, which are sometimes wrong, especially for smaller crops.
gaps.sensorChange: Bare-day numbers use satellite data from 2013 on. Older and newer satellites aren't matched yet, so treat them as estimates.

risks.lateKill: {crops}: killing it late in spring can use up soil moisture the next crop needs. Terminate on time.
risks.thirstyDryland: {crops} need a lot of water for dryland.
risks.heat: {crops} can suffer in heat. {count} of {total} years here were hot or drought years.
risks.contractCrop: {crops}: grown by contract only and not a common crop in this region. Check with a buyer and your county agent.
risks.coverEstablish: {crops}: the bare-day estimate assumes the cover crop establishes. In a dry fall it may not.

confidence.longClimate: {count} years of climate data for your field.
confidence.goodHistory: {count} years of crop history from satellite maps.
confidence.familiarCrops: Most crops have been grown on this field before.
confidence.someNewCrops: Some crops are new to this field.
confidence.newCrops: Most crops are new to this field.
confidence.placeholderTraits: Crop trait values are early estimates and still being checked.
confidence.modelStrong: The crop model was right {acc}% of the time on years it never saw ({bal}% balanced across crops).
confidence.modelMixed: The crop model was right {acc}% of the time on years it never saw, but only {bal}% balanced across crops.
confidence.datasetsAgree: Two rain datasets agree for this field (correlation {corr}, {pct}% apart).
confidence.datasetsDisagree: Two rain datasets disagree for this field (correlation {corr}, {pct}% apart).
confidence.coarseWeather: Weather data covers a wide area (about 30 miles), not just your field.

ndvi.title: NDVI (plant greenness)
ndvi.text: Satellites measure how green the ground looks, from 0 (bare dirt) to 1 (thick green crop). Below 0.25 we count the month as bare.

soilMoisture.title: Soil moisture
soilMoisture.text: How wet or dry the top of the soil was compared with a normal year. Measured from space by NASA's SMAP satellite.

hydrologicGroup.title: Hydrologic group
hydrologicGroup.text: How fast rain soaks into your soil. Group A soaks in fastest. Group D is slowest, so more rain runs off the field.

coverCrop.title: Cover crop
coverCrop.text: A crop grown mainly to protect and feed the soil between cash crops, like cereal rye or hairy vetch.

slope.title: Slope
slope.text: How steep your field is. On steeper ground, rain washes soil away faster. Measured from a NASA elevation map.

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.text: How sure we are about a score. It is higher when we have many years of data and the crops have grown on your field before.

score.title: Score
score.text: A number from 0 to 100 for how well a rotation fits your goals and limits. Your chosen goals count double. Every rule is open for experts to check.

bareDays.title: Bare days
bareDays.text: Days when satellites saw little or no plant cover, so the soil was open to wind and rain.

heldOut.title: Tested on unseen years
heldOut.text: We hid one year at a time from the model, trained it on the others, and checked its answer for the hidden year. This shows how it does on a year it has never seen, like next year.

bareScore.title: Ground cover score
bareScore.text: 100 minus the share of the year the ground was bare. 100 means plants or residue all year. Lower means more bare days, when soil can wash or blow away.

si.title: How sure are the models?
si.intro: Each model was tested only on years it never saw while learning.
si.cropLine: right {acc}% of the time ({bal}% balanced across crops). Guessing “same as last year” is right {base}%.
si.fieldAgree: On this field: matched the crop map in {pct}% of years.
si.stressLine: low confidence. Weather explains only a small part of crop stress (R² {r2}).
si.stressCrops: Shown only for crops where it beat “assume a normal year”: {crops}.
si.yearLine: the same drought / wet / heat / normal label {pct}% of the time ({from}–{to}).
si.cardTitle: What the models saw on this field
si.cardAccuracy: Crop model on unseen years: {acc}% right, {bal}% balanced across crops.
si.noModel: {crop}: no satellite model for this crop yet.
si.recognized: {crop}: recognized from space in {n} of {of} years it was grown here.
si.neverGrown: {crop}: not grown on this field since 2008.
si.hardToSee: Hard crop to recognize: only {pct}% found on unseen years.
si.riskSignal: Weather risk signal (low confidence): flagged {n} of {of} seasons.
si.riskNoSeasons: Weather risk signal: no seasons since 2015 to check.
si.riskNotForCrop: Weather alone doesn’t predict stress well for this crop.

replay.drySoil: Soil moisture in {year} was {pct}% drier than normal.
replay.hot: {year} had {days} days of 95 °F or hotter here (normal is about {avg}).
replay.wetYear: {year} was {pct}% wetter than normal, so heavy rain could wash bare soil away.

replay.coverPartial: Dry-year rule: {crops} counted as only half established, because a dry fall can stop cover crops from coming up.

replayUi.title: Replay a bad year
replayUi.caption: Pick a real past year. We re-score every option under that year's actual weather on your field.
replayUi.vsNormal: {n} points {dir} than in a normal year
replayUi.heading: If {year} came back
replayUi.note: This is a stress check from real weather and crop traits, not a yield forecast. Local experts know your field best.
replayUi.glanceTitle: How each option holds up in {year}
replayUi.see: See how rotations hold up in {year}
replayUi.noYear: No weather record for {year} on this field.
replayUi.coverRule: In drought years we count cover crops as only half established, so their bare-day savings are halved. A dry fall can stop them from coming up, and we don't want the replay to oversell them.

bareUi.stripAltNone: No month is usually bare under this rotation.
bareUi.stripTitle: Chance the ground is bare, by month
bareUi.calibrated: Uses this field's own satellite record for {crops}. Regional patterns for the rest.
bareUi.regional: Regional patterns. This field has too few years of these crops to use its own record.
bareUi.caveat: An estimate from satellite crop calendars, not a measurement. Bare days from before 2013 aren't used because the satellites changed.
bareUi.coverAssumption: Assumes the cover crop establishes. In a dry fall it may not.
bareUi.fallowNote: Bare fallow is our estimate for a tilled field. Satellite “fallow” fields are often weedy, so they don't show it.
